claims.hypothesis: NH2CHO, CH3OH, and H2CO in the disk atmosphere are thermally desorbed from the ice mantle on dust grains.
claims.experiment: Compare the observed outer emission radii of NH2CHO, CH3OH, and H2CO derived from PV diagrams against their computed binding energies on amorphous solid water ice.
claims.result: The outer emission radius increases from ~ 24 au for NH2CHO, to 40 au for CH3OH, and to 48 au for H2CO, matching the decreasing order of their binding energies.
claims.finding: The sequence of outer radii is consistent with decreasing binding energies, supporting that NH2CHO, CH3OH, and H2CO are thermally desorbed from ice mantles.

evidence.quote: More importantly, we find that the increasing order of the outer emission radius of NH$_2$CHO, CH$_3$OH, and H$_2$CO is consistent with the decreasing order of their binding energies, supporting that they are thermally desorbed from the ice mantle on dust grains.

claims.hypothesis: HNCO is the parent species of NH2CHO on dust grains or in the gas phase.
claims.experiment: Compare the spatial distribution, kinematics, excitation temperature, and binding energy of HNCO with those of NH2CHO.
claims.result: Despite having a much lower binding energy than NH2CHO, HNCO has the same outer radius (~ 24 au), kinematics, and excitation temperature (~ 231 K vs ~ 221 K) as NH2CHO, and is absent in the cooler outer disk.
claims.finding: HNCO is more likely a daughter species formed in the gas phase from desorbed NH2CHO rather than its parent molecule.

evidence.quote: We also find that HNCO, which has much lower binding energy than NH$_2$CHO, has almost the same spatial distribution, kinematics, and temperature as NH$_2$CHO, and is thus more likely a daughter species of desorbed NH$_2$CHO.
Thus, our result implies that HNCO, instead of being parent molecule, is likely a daughter molecule of NH$_2$CHO and formed in gas phase.

claims.hypothesis: H2CO is the gas-phase parent molecule of NH2CHO via the reaction H2CO + NH2 -> NH2CHO + H.
claims.experiment: Compare the spatial distribution and kinematics of H2CO and NH2CHO in the disk atmosphere.
claims.result: H2CO has a much more extended spatial distribution (outer radius ~ 48 au and extending into the disk wind) and different kinematics compared to NH2CHO (outer radius ~ 24 au).
claims.finding: It is questionable and unclear whether H2CO can be the gas-phase parent molecule of NH2CHO, though lack of information on NH2 (whose parent NH3 has a higher binding energy than H2CO) prevents a definitive conclusion.

evidence.quote: On the other hand, we find that H$_2$CO has a more extended spatial distribution with different kinematics from NH$_2$CHO, thus questioning whether it can be the gas-phase parent molecule of NH$_2$CHO.
In conclusion, based on the current observations, it is not possible to constrain the formation route of formamide in the disk atmosphere of HH 212.

why_this_data.value: Band 6 (~ 1.33 mm) covers more NH2CHO lines along with HNCO, H2CO, D2CO, H2(13)CO, CH3OH, and CH3CHO, and has lower dust continuum optical depth than 0.85 mm, allowing molecular line mapping closer to the midplane and central source.

evidence.quote: Here we map it at a longer wavelength $\lambda \sim$ 1.33 mm, with spectral windows set up to cover more NH$_2$CHO lines in order to derive the physical properties of NH$_2$CHO.
At longer wavelength, since the continuum emission of the disk is optically thinner, we can also map the molecular line emission in the disk atmosphere closer to the midplane and the central source.

why_this_method.value: Lines were stacked into two E_u bins to increase sensitivity for better detections; non-LTE LVG was used for CH3OH lines with E_u < 200 K because they are optically thick and previous LTE rotation diagram estimates were overestimated.

evidence.quote: In order to increase the sensitivity for better detections, we divided them into 2 ranges of upper level energies: $E_u < 120$ K and $E_u > 120 K$, and then stacked them to produce the mean channel maps

evidence.loc: Physical Properties in the Disk Atmosphere
evidence.quote: More importantly, the excitation temperature was also overestimated because almost all the lines had E$_u$ $<$ 200 K and were thus likely optically thick.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: HNCO and HCOOH coming from the decomposition of desorbed organic salts (NH4+OCN- and NH4+HCOO-) which have binding energies similar to NH2CHO.

evidence.loc: Distribution of Molecules and Binding Energy
evidence.quote: On the other hand, HNCO and HCOOH may come from the decomposition of the desorbed organic salts (NH$_4^+$OCN$^-$ and NH$_4^+$HCOO$^-$), which have similar BE to that of NH$_2$CHO (cite: Kruckiewicz2021; Ligterink2018).

limitations_admitted.value: Higher spectral and spatial resolution observations are needed to verify the possible ~ 0.5 km s^-1 velocity shift (infall/accretion) between the upper and lower disk atmospheres for NH2CHO/HNCO/t-HCOOH.

evidence.quote: Note that for NH$_2$CHO/HNCO/t-HCOOH, there seems to be a small velocity shift of $\sim$ 0.5 km s$^{-1}$ between the upper and lower disk atmosphere. This velocity shift could suggest an infall (or accretion) velocity of $\sim$ 0.25 km s$^{-1}$, which is $\sim$ 8% of the rotation velocity at $\sim$ 24 au. However, observations at higher spectral and spatial resolution are needed to verify this possibility.

limitations_admitted.value: Excitation temperatures of H2CO, D2CO, H2(13)CO, and CH3CHO cannot be derived from rotation diagrams due to narrow E_u range (< 120 K), few detected lines, and optical thickness, requiring assumed temperatures.

evidence.loc: Physical Properties in the Disk Atmosphere
evidence.quote: On the other hand, since H$_2$CO, D$_2$CO, and CH$_3$CHO are only detected with a narrow range of $E_u < 120$ K and their emission can be optically thick there, we can not derive their excitation temperature from the rotation diagram.

limitations_admitted.value: Excitation temperatures derived for NH2CHO and HNCO have large uncertainties (~ 226 +/- 130 K).

evidence.loc: Physical Properties in the Disk Atmosphere
evidence.quote: It is interesting to note that NH$_2$CHO and HNCO have roughly the same excitation temperature of $\sim$ $226\pm130$ K, although with a large uncertainty.

limitations_admitted.value: Lack of observational information on NH2 prevents constraining whether the gas-phase reaction H2CO + NH2 -> NH2CHO + H is responsible for formamide formation.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, we have no information on the other reactant, NH$_2$.
In conclusion, based on the current observations, it is not possible to constrain the formation route of formamide in the disk atmosphere of HH 212.

referee_caveats_inferred: Molecular abundances depend directly on the H2 column density adopted from an external dusty disk model (Lee et al. 2021b) rather than a direct gas mass tracer.
Column densities for H2CO, D2CO, H2(13)CO, and CH3CHO rely on fixed, assumed excitation temperatures (60 K, 92 K, 100 K).
Line intensities are assumed to have a uniform 40% uncertainty, which dominates the error bars on derived column densities and temperatures.

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00712.S.

missing_for_reproduction: Exact coordinates of the phase center, the CH3OH peak pixel, the 0.17" x 0.05" rectangular extraction region, and the PV cut axes
Details of the line stacking procedure (e.g., weighting, velocity alignment, and channel interpolation)
GRELVG code availability and exact input files
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: moderate (~10-50 GB for two Band 6 execution blocks with 46 antennas and cuatro 1920-channel spectral windows)
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project code, calibration CASA version, calibrators, robust weightings, synthesized beams, noise levels, and complete line tables with integrated intensities are clearly provided, allowing direct reproduction of the rotation diagrams; however, imaging parameters, line stacking details, exact extraction region coordinates, and the GRELVG code are not fully specified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data (2017.1.00712.S) with a clear set of 47 spectral lines in Table 1, explicit integrated line intensities, and well-defined quantitative outputs (outer radii, vertical heights, excitation temperatures, and column densities in Table 2).

methods_papers.why: Initial development of the GRELVG code used for non-LTE LVG modeling of CH3OH
Rotation diagram method under optically thin and LTE assumptions

companion_papers.why: Previous Band 7 (0.85 mm) detection of COMs and NH2CHO in the HH 212 disk atmosphere
Previous ~ 346 GHz COM observations of HH 212 providing t-HCOOH data and [CH2DOH]/[CH3OH] ratio
Dusty disk model of HH 212 used for H2 column density, temperature structure, and dust optical depth
